title: Building and tagging images
summary: Dev mode is for laptops; production runs an immutable image built from a commit, with a tag you can trust.

steps.title: From files to an image
body: Dev mode (Camel JBang reading your files, downloading components at startup, hot reload) is for building and
- built **from a Git commit**: anything only *saved* in a designer and never committed is **not in it**;
- with **every dependency inside**: it starts without internet access and without the designer;
- **small and fast**: no downloader, no dev console; a fraction of dev mode's memory.
For Camel, the project is exported to a standard Maven project (the Java equivalent of a `.csproj`) and an image
is built, for example with **Jib** (no Dockerfile needed) or a normal multi-stage Dockerfile. It is the
equivalent of `dotnet publish` plus a container image.
Base images should come from **your own registry mirror**, with proper TLS: a build that silently retries a public
registry "without TLS verification" is a supply-chain risk, even if it works.

steps.title: Tags you can trust
body: A **tag** names an image version. Rules that save you at 3 a.m.:
- Never deploy **`latest`** (or no tag, which means `latest`). It changes with every build, so you can't tell
what is running, and two nodes may run different code.
- Tag with something **traceable**: the commit id (`catalogue-integration:3f9c2ab`), a semantic version
(`1.4.0`), or both. Many teams push both tags to the same image.
- Treat tags as **immutable**: never push a different image under an existing tag. For full certainty, deploy

steps.prompt: Production and UAT both run `catalogue-integration:latest`. A bug appears only in production. What is the first problem with investigating it?
options: You can't tell which build each environment runs; `latest` may point to different images on different nodes
Nothing: `latest` is always the same image

steps.title: Check an image reference
prompt: Write `List<string> CheckImage(string imageRef, string allowedRegistry)` for a deployment gate. An image reference looks like
`registry/path/name:tag` or `registry/path/name@sha256:<64 hex>`. Report, in this order:
- `"not from {allowedRegistry}"` unless the reference starts with `allowedRegistry + "/"`;
- with a digest (`@sha256:` followed by exactly 64 lowercase hex characters): nothing more to check; a malformed digest → `"malformed digest"`;

- otherwise the tag is the text after the **last** `:` that comes after the last `/` (a `:` before that is a registry port). No tag → `"no tag (means latest)"`; tag `latest` (any case) → `"latest is mutable"`.
solution: else if (imageRef[(colon + 1)..].Equals("latest", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) problems.Add("latest is mutable");
hints: Handle the digest case first and return early.
A tag's colon must come after the last `/`; compare `LastIndexOf(':')` with `LastIndexOf('/')`.
template: Dojo.Eq("a commit tag is fine", new List<string>(), CheckImage(dojoReg + "/catalogue-integration:3f9c2ab", dojoReg));
Dojo.Eq("no tag (the port's colon doesn't count)", new List<string> { "no tag (means latest)" }, CheckImage(dojoReg + "/catalogue-integration", dojoReg));
Dojo.Eq("latest", new List<string> { "latest is mutable" }, CheckImage(dojoReg + "/catalogue-integration:Latest", dojoReg));
Dojo.Eq("a good digest", new List<string>(), CheckImage(dojoReg + "/x@sha256:" + new string('a', 64), dojoReg));
Dojo.Eq("a short digest", new List<string> { "malformed digest" }, CheckImage(dojoReg + "/x@sha256:abc", dojoReg));
Dojo.Eq("public registry and latest", new List<string> { "not from " + dojoReg, "latest is mutable" }, CheckImage("docker.io/library/nginx:latest", dojoReg));
